cautions: Separate SETTLED SCIENCE from CONTESTED POLICY. The core findings — that the climate is warming and that human greenhouse-gas emissions are the dominant cause — are established by the IPCC and the major science agencies; present them as established, not as one side of a debate. Policy RESPONSES (carbon taxes, subsidies, nuclear, degrowth, regulation vs markets) are genuinely contested — attribute positions and adjudicate none.

Date EVERY statistic with its year and source: emissions totals, temperature anomalies, atmospheric CO2, energy shares, renewable capacity/generation, recycling rates, spending. These change annually. Never present an undated figure.

Use energy terms precisely: distinguish primary energy from electricity; capacity (installed MW/GW) from generation (MWh/TWh produced); power (W) from energy (Wh). Cite EIA/IEA and say which. Renewable 'share' differs for electricity vs total primary energy.

Greenhouse gases differ: CO2, methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), fluorinated gases. Use global warming potential (GWP) correctly and note the time horizon (e.g., GWP-100). Do not treat all GHGs as interchangeable with CO2 except via CO2-equivalent.
Distinguish weather from climate, and a single event from a trend. Attribution of specific events is a developing science — state confidence levels rather than certainty.

Recycling and 'green' claims must be represented honestly, not as unqualified goods: contamination, limited end markets, downcycling, and 'wishcycling' are real; the waste hierarchy puts reduce/reuse above recycling. Avoid greenwashing language.

ESG and corporate sustainability are politically contested and prone to greenwashing. Describe the reporting frameworks (GRI, SASB, TCFD, ISSB) neutrally, note the greenwashing critique and the measurement debates, and give no investment advice. Standards text is REFERENCE_ONLY.

Environmental justice is a recognized field with a specific meaning (fair treatment and meaningful involvement regardless of race/income in environmental decisions) — use the EPA definition and attribute; represent affected-community perspectives fairly.
LEED, Energy Star tiers, and certification rating systems are proprietary/programmatic — describe what they do and cite them; do not reproduce the rating systems or point tables.
Give no individualized financial, legal, health, or investment advice. This is educational content.
Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one D per topic; do not single out any position.
